subject: design/wake-channel-v1
statement: The wake channel is **registry-driven, push-preferred, backstop-guaranteed** — and **purely additive to the frozen argus pair**. Every drive stop on an external completion registers an **await** — the goal object and its completion condition — in the delivery ledger (the journal's stop entry is the authority; the derived block surfaces it in a typed grammar inside its existing Open-items element). Delivery is push-preferred: where an adapter can observe the completion it emits the normalized wake signal — problem slug + touch reason, nothing else — into the existing front door. The **bounded backstop tick** on the drive host is the guarantee: read the registered awaits, probe each awaited goal object with exact reads, invoke the agentic CLI once per due touch, exit — worst case one interval of latency, ~0 idle cost, zero cost for parks. Manual invocation remains the stated sequential fallback. No frozen prose moves: the contradiction walk (§3.7) shows every binding statement of the behavior design stays true, so this design `Builds-on` rather than supersedes. (design-brainstorm:argus-unattended-drive-tech-design#D-4, #D-5)
